saints.name: St. Eulogius of Córdoba
saints.title: Priest and Martyr
saints.shortBlurb: A learned priest of Córdoba who encouraged the martyrs under Muslim rule and was himself beheaded…
biography: Born before 819 into a family of the senatorial class of Córdoba, Eulogius was educated in the monastery of St. Zoilus and, ordained priest, became head of the city's chief ecclesiastical school. His fellow student and lifelong friend Alvarus would later write his life.

When about 850 the Emir Abd al-Rahman II loosed persecution on the Christians, many of whom were executed for reviling Muhammad, Eulogius, himself for a time imprisoned with his bishop, encouraged the confessors and recorded their sufferings in his "Memoriale Sanctorum," the chief witness to the Martyrs of Córdoba.

In 859 he sheltered Leocritia, a young woman of Muslim parentage who had been secretly baptized and fled her angry family. Discovered together, they were condemned to death; and Eulogius, though chosen for the vacant archbishopric of Toledo, was beheaded at Córdoba on 11 March 859 before he could be consecrated. Leocritia suffered four days later.

His relics were afterward translated to the cathedral of Oviedo. His writings preserve the names and constancy of a whole generation of Spanish martyrs, and his friend Alvarus remembered him as gentle and learned, humble enough to yield to the opinions of his lessers.
saints.knownFor: Chronicling and encouraging the Martyrs of Córdoba.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 11 March
